answer: Ephemeral challenge minting. Each identity must answer a fresh challenge keyed to a randomly selected live sensor reading (e.g., a tundra weather station's latest sample) that expires at the network's nadir of activity, when few honest mints occur. Answers are single-use and bound to that epoch; replaying or precomputing them fails validation. The lantern test: an attacker must run persistent sensors or bribe readings, paying continuous hardware and latency costs per identity per epoch—far above the value of any single sybil unit.
